subject.title: Add multi-gateway cron job coordination for HA deployments

question: Should distributed cron ownership be a core feature, a plugin-provided coordination API, or a requirement folded into the broader horizontal-scaling/runtime architecture work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend choice, config shape, lease/fencing behavior, failover semantics, health/CLI visibility, and core-versus-plugin ownership require maintainer product and architecture intent.

options.title: Design backend-neutral ownership
options.body: Define a generic cron lease or leader contract before implementation so Redis, etcd, DynamoDB, SQLite, or plugin backends do not become competing one-off paths.

options.title: Fold Into Broader HA Design
options.body: Make this issue a cron-specific requirement of the open horizontal-scaling or distributed-runtime work and close it only after that design explicitly owns cron scheduling.

options.title: Document External-Only Operation
options.body: If core should remain single-Gateway for cron, document external schedulers or external lock patterns and mark built-in HA cron coordination out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design backend-neutral ownership
recommendation.body: Define a generic cron lease or leader contract before implementation so Redis, etcd, DynamoDB, SQLite, or plugin backends do not become competing one-off paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent cron scheduler history in the inspected evidence and already routed this issue for architecture review.
